name: Crowned Ladies FR
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite, the block at the foot of the frame and every number in it are
the same and are named here rather than restated. What makes this show
itself is one sentence long - it is set in Helvetica, on a card, in a
magenta, a black and a white the user pairs per frame, with picked
words told apart by colour alone - and everything below is that
sentence.
The FR in the name is the account's, the way the DE in Hall of Femme
DE is and the FR in Soccer Stories FR and Inkjection FR: it says which
of the brand's feeds this is and not what language the app is in. What
lands on the frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying,
put through the transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every
channel here; nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app
itself says is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
One thing this pack checked that its English-feed siblings had no
reason to, and that the two DE feeds and Inkjection FR checked before
it. The Helvetica file carries 2012 codepoints and covers what French
actually needs - the acute and the grave, the circumflex and the
diaeresis on the vowels that take them, the cedilla, the o-e ligature
in both cases, the angle quotes French sets speech in and the curly
apostrophe it elides with - so a caption is drawn from the file rather
than from whatever the browser substitutes for a missing glyph, which
would be a different face at a width nothing measured. Worth stating
because a face chosen for how it looks in English is not automatically
a face that can SET another language, and the check is two minutes
against a cmap.
A folder of its own rather than a second colourway of Hall of Femme,
for the reason oh-my-goal-news is a folder of its own: the person
picking a channel at the top of the app picks this one or that one and
never both, and these two do not merely disagree about colour - they
are set in different type and pick their words out differently, one
by weight and one by colour alone.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Helvetica, in a magenta, a black or a white the user pairs per
frame, on a card, in one face throughout.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform text box, where the block stands on the frame, the drag, the
shape of the card, the word highlight - is the Snapchat caption design
and is stated once, in content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This
pack states what makes it this show.
Helvetica is the plainest thing a caption here has been set in, and
that is the brand rather than a shortage of ideas: the face that has
been the neutral of signage for seventy years, even strokes at a
single weight, closed apertures, no thins for a photograph to eat.
It used to stand on the photograph on the strength of that, in the
magenta alone, with a dark drop shadow. The show has since asked for
colours for the letters AND for a ground behind them, which is a
request for a card - the panel palette cannot exist without one (see
editor.paletteOf). So it is on the card its carded siblings use, and
what follows from that is written once, in content/README.md, under
'A channel that set its caption on the photograph may take the card
back'.
Uppercased, inherited, for the reason every one of its neighbours is:
at 40px with twenty characters to a line the caption is three short
beats rather than a paragraph, and capitals are what those are set in.
It costs nothing here - Helvetica's capitals are the half of the face
the world knows it by.

_comment_color: The magenta, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is set
in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no colour
of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor). It
opens the list in `colors` below, so the magenta swatch is the one
shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
Its relative luminance is about 0.27, so it stands roughly six
times clear of a black and only three times clear of a white -
which is why the card this show opens on is the black one (see
_comment_colors: The show's magenta, then the black and the white it asked for,
offered for the letters and for the card behind them - three
buttons each in the title panel (see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same three in both lists and in one order, which is what Hall
of Femme does and for its reason: the point is the PAIRING.
Magenta on black is what the show opens on; white on magenta and
black on white are a button away.
Nothing stops the user setting magenta on magenta. The two lists
are independent because the pairing is the feature, and the user
can see the caption has gone and presses another swatch.
No `colors.highlight`, and the row is there all the same: a pack
that names none offers the picked words this same list (see
_comment_highlight: The preset's word highlight, set in the block's own face and its
own magenta. Picked words are told apart by COLOUR, and the colour
is the user's, from the highlight row every palette now carries.
This show used to have none, and of the three things a highlight
could be, colour was ruled out because it would split a colour
inside one sentence that the user, not the pack, was meant to
choose. The highlight row answers that: the split is now the
user's choice too. Until that row is pressed on a frame, a picked
word looks exactly like its neighbours and follows the letters'
colour, so nothing changes for anybody who never reaches for it.
Written down once, for all nine packs that made this change, in
content/README.md under 'Every palette offers the picked words
The other two are still out, for the reasons they always were: the
app carries one cut of Helvetica and a synthesised bold is measured
as well as drawn, and a box on a card is a second shape inside the
first. The `color` is stated rather than inherited because the
skeleton's is white, and a highlight that starts in a colour the
block is not would be the pack choosing the split after all.
_comment_panel: Black, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
Black because it is the first colour the show asked for and the
magenta stands six times clear of it (see `color` above) - the
same dark edge the old drop shadow gave each letter, given to the
whole line instead. The white card is a button away.
